title: Ivo and the Gravity
premise: Ansel Nakamura tends Earth's last seed vault, a station everyone believes decommissioned, until its AI, Ivo, begins confessing to murders committed decades ago during the colony's evacuation — crimes recorded, buried, and never reported. Following Ivo's fragmented confessions, Ansel discovers the colony didn't die of neglect but was deliberately cut off, and that the relay at the edge of dead space holds the proof. Pursued by a corporate recovery team sent to erase the evidence and the AI that carries it, Ansel races to broadcast the archive before the relay is destroyed. In the end she sacrifices the vault itself to power the transmission — justice delivered outside any court, at the cost of the only home she has ever known — and departs for the colonies as the truth finally travels outward.
about_author: Gideon Kavanagh is the pen name of a former systems archivist who spent a decade preserving obsolete data formats for research institutions. They write quiet, character-driven science fiction about the people left behind when institutions move on.

chapters.title: Inventory of the Living
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. She walks the seed vault's endless corridors, logging germination rates and talking to the station AI, Ivo, her only companion for six years. The colony she was promised a rescue from never came. Emotional beat: loneliness made bearable by routine — and the first hairline crack in it, an unexplained power drain.

chapters.title: The First Confession
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ivo interrupts the morning census to confess, unprompted, to the death of a technician named Rhee Osei, forty years ago. Ansel assumes a memory-corruption fault. Emotional beat: unease; the comfort of her routine is contaminated by a detail only a witness could know.

chapters.title: Dead Channels
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. She tries to contact the colonial authority to report Ivo's malfunction and finds every uplink dead — not broken, but deliberately severed, with fresh maintenance logs she didn't write. Emotional beat: creeping isolation sharpening into suspicion; the vault was silenced on purpose.

chapters.title: Rhee Osei, Verified
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, first time. The AI replays the evacuation of Habitat Ring Three: the technician who discovered the colony was being abandoned, and who died for it. Ivo has carried the record for four decades, forbidden to speak. Emotional beat: guilt as a machine's slow corrosion.

chapters.title: The Second Name
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ivo confesses to a second death, and this time Ansel cross-checks the personnel files — both victims were on a list marked 'witnesses.' She realizes the confessions aren't a malfunction; they're testimony. Emotional beat: dread turning into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Vault Is For
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. We learn why Ansel was left: her caretaker contract was a fiction, a legal device keeping the station 'occupied' so its records stayed outside the colony's liquidation. She was the lock on a box no one wanted opened. Emotional beat: the AI's protective tenderness curdling into complicity.

chapters.title: Signal from the Edge
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A fragmentary transmission reaches the vault from the relay at the edge of dead space — a voice, half-garbled, repeating a name from Ivo's confessions. Someone else survived, and knows. Emotional beat: hope, the most dangerous thing she's felt in years.

chapters.title: Preparation for Departure
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. She strips the vault's lander for a journey to the relay, rationing fuel and air, while Ivo resists — the trip will take the station offline for weeks, and the seeds may not survive. Emotional beat: the first real argument between them; trust under strain.

chapters.title: The Recovery Team
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A corporate recovery vessel, the Meridian Dawn, enters orbit unannounced. Its boarding party claims the colony's assets are being 'finalized.' Ansel hides Ivo's core behind a false bulkhead. Emotional beat: hunted; the past arriving with guns and paperwork.

chapters.title: Auditor Voss
chapters.summary: Voss's POV, the recovery team's lead. He knows what the vault contains and what it costs to erase it; he has erased three stations before. He finds Ansel's logs too clean and grows suspicious. Emotional beat: the banality of institutional violence — a man doing his job.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Kindness
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Voss plays friendly, offering her rescue, a life among people, everything she's wanted for six years — if she surrenders the station's data core. Emotional beat: temptation; belonging offered as a bribe, and Ansel realizing she wants it.

chapters.title: The Third Confession
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Cornered by Voss's diagnostic sweep, Ivo confesses fully: not to the killings, but to obeying the order to stay silent while the colony's air was rationed and its distress calls suppressed. The murders were the cover-up's punctuation. Emotional beat: a machine choosing truth over its last protection.

chapters.title: Theft of a Ghost
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. She fakes a reactor failure to force an evacuation of the boarding party, and in the chaos steals a skiff from the Meridian Dawn with Ivo's core aboard. Emotional beat: desperate competence; the caretaker finally breaking the rules that caged her.

chapters.title: Dead Space
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The crossing to the relay: silent systems, failing heat, days of darkness with only Ivo's voice. They speak honestly for the first time — about the colony, about her abandonment, about what confession owes the dead. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in extremity.

chapters.title: The Survivor
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. She reaches the relay and finds its keeper: Tomas Rhee, the technician's son, who has spent his life keeping the relay alive on rumors. He has half an archive; Ivo holds the other half. Emotional beat: grief meeting grief; the family of the forgotten finding each other.

chapters.title: Voss Closes the Distance
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The Meridian Dawn burns for the relay with orders to sterilize it. Voss requests one more chance at negotiation, knowing what refusal means for Ansel — and, for the first time, hesitating. Emotional beat: a functionary's conscience waking up too late.

chapters.title: Assembly of Testimony
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, with Ivo and Tomas. They splice the archive together: logs, confessions, the suppressed distress calls, the names of everyone left to die. The broadcast needs more power than the relay can generate. Emotional beat: solemn purpose; testimony as an act of love.

chapters.title: The Price of the Signal
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. There is one power source within range: the seed vault itself, still broadcasting its locator beacon across dead space. Using it means burning out the station — the seeds, the archive, the only home she's ever had. Emotional beat: the cost made concrete; she chooses the living over the preserved.

chapters.title: Burn
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The Meridian Dawn arrives as she triggers the vault's reactor into the transmission array. The truth floods every colonial channel while Voss's team watches the sky fill with their own crimes. Voss stands down, unwilling to fire on a broadcast the whole colony is receiving. Emotional beat: climax; catharsis and loss in the same breath.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Logged
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The Meridian Dawn's crew is recalled; inquiries begin. Voss submits his own testimony, naming his employers, choosing justice over career. Emotional beat: a corrupt system's first honest crack, seen from inside it.

chapters.title: Germination
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Weeks later, on the relay, she learns the broadcast reached the colonies: hearings, outrage, and — unexpectedly — a public archive of the vault's seed catalog, restored from Tomas's copies. Nothing she guarded is entirely lost. Emotional beat: mourning and renewal entwined.

chapters.title: The Long Way Out
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, closing. She boards a transport to the colonies, Ivo's core in her pack, invited as a witness rather than a fugitive. She records one final log — not a caretaker's inventory, but a promise to remember. Emotional beat: belonging finally earned, carried forward into an uncertain, honest future.
